capabilities: look up words by hovering or selecting text in notes and text-based PDFs
translate selected sentences with an OpenAI-compatible AI service
import TXT/CSV/Excel/DOCX word lists and study them in five modes with SM-2 scheduling
visualize difficult words as dandelion clusters or a 3D particle nebula
import MDX/JSON/JS dictionaries and sync saved words to Eudic
extras: The plugin UI is currently in Chinese; full English documentation is in README_EN.md. The README explains its use of Node.js file access and child_process (PowerShell OCR on Windows only) for community review, states there is no telemetry, and documents every remote service it may contact.
motivation: The author wanted to chain looking up, memorizing, reviewing, and playing into one loop instead of isolated dictionary popups: "词忆不是「查词弹窗」的堆砌，而是把 查 → 记 → 复习 → 玩 串成闭环".
problem: Obsidian has no built-in dictionary, translation, or vocabulary review, so learners must leave their notes to look up and memorize words.
